newsitem.title: UK: Waterford offer worth 290 mln punts-FT.
newsitem.headline: Waterford offer worth 290 mln punts-FT.

text.p: Ireland's Avonmore Foods Plc launched a one-for-two share offer for Waterfood Foods on Sunday worth nearly 290 million Irish pounds, or 117-1/2p a share based on Avonmore's share price on Friday, the Financial Times said.
A further 68 million Irish pounds is being offered for preference shares and at least 36 million Irish pounds in bonuses to farmers via milk prices, the report said.
On Friday Waterford had announced that it had received an approach from Avonmore and was in talks but gave no further details.
If Avonmore succeeds, the combined turnover of the new group would be in excess of 2.5 billion Irish pounds and elevate the new Irish agri-company to the world stage, analysts had said.

Analysts said the synergies between the two companies were considerable and would create major economies of scale and opportunites for rationalisation since both were involved in the dairy industry and in trading animal feeds and fertilizers.
They said Avonmore's chances of succeeding after failing in a similar attempt in 1991 were greatly enhanced by the fact that Waterford had had a very tough year.
Waterford's profits and share price have plummeted with margins squeezed by lower butter and milk prices amid internal wrangling and a serious shake-up in its management structure.
